Interface PanelElement

All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractPanelElement, Button, Checkbox, Divider, Dropdown, DropdownMulti, Flow, HudIcon, HudSlot, Icon, InfoBox, ItemDisplay, ProgressBar, Radio, ScrollContainer, Section, Slider, SlotElement, SlotFlowElement, Tabs, TextField, TextLabel, Toggle
public interface PanelElement
A visual or interactive element within a Panel. Elements are positioned absolutely within the panel's content area (after padding) using childX/childY coordinates.

Panel elements are a decorative/interactive layer on top of the panel backgrounds. In inventory-menu panels they sit alongside slot groups (which live on the handler, not on the panel itself); in HUD panels and standalone-screen panels they are the only content.

Elements are per-panel-instance: each panel holds its own elements. Elements aren't shared between panels.

MenuKit's own elements are built with builders and extend AbstractPanelElement (§0066). Consumer mods can implement this interface directly for custom element types.

Coordinate contract

Two coordinate spaces are in play across the element surface:
  • Panel-local: getChildX() / getChildY() specify the element's position within the panel's content area (after padding).
  • Screen-space: absolute coordinates in the game window's GUI-scaled pixel grid. RenderContext and InputContext carry the content origin and the mouse in screen space.
Render and input compose the two the same way: the element's top-left is (ctx.originX() + getChildX(), ctx.originY() + getChildY()).

Input receives its context (§0066)

Every input method takes an InputContext, as render(RenderContext) takes a RenderContext: the content origin, the mouse, and whether the element's panel or container is disabled. An element never caches its origin or its hover state from the last frame. The one dispatcher (the panel's host, or a container through ChildDispatch) hit-tests before it calls mouseClicked(InputContext, int) and mouseScrolled(InputContext, double, double), and does not deliver clicks, wheel or keys at all in a disabled context.

  • Method Details

    • getChildX

    • getChildY

    • getWidth

      int getWidth()
      Width in pixels.

    • getHeight

      int getHeight()
      Height in pixels.

    • fillWidth

      default void fillWidth(int width)
      Stretches this element to fill the given content width (the CrossAlign.FILL column-fill primitive). After this call the element's getWidth() reports the filled width so panel auto-size, hit-testing, and rendering all agree.

      Default: no-op. AbstractPanelElement re-authors its width here; intrinsic widgets (an icon, a checkbox square, a sprite switch) keep their size.

      Parameters:
      width - the column's widest-child extent to stretch to, in pixels

    • naturalWidth

      default int naturalWidth()
      The element's NATURAL (authored / intrinsic) width before any panel width-constraint: what it wants when the panel has room. The owning Panel maxes this across its elements to compute its hug-width, then feeds each element a budget via layoutWithin(int). Distinct from getWidth(), which reports the resolved width. Default returns getWidth().

    • layoutWithin

      default void layoutWithin(int budget)
      Width flows DOWN: the owning Panel (or container) calls this every layout pass with the horizontal pixel budget available to this element. The element resolves its presentation width, and when it wraps a label its height, REVERSIBLY from its authored intent: a later call with a larger budget restores the natural extent.
      • Text-bearing elements wrap their text to the budget, growing taller (reported through extraLayoutHeight()).
      • Fixed controls (Slider, TextField, ProgressBar, a Dropdown's trigger) cap their width to the budget.
      • A filling Divider takes the whole budget.
      • Intrinsic widgets ignore it.

      Default: no-op.

      Parameters:
      budget - horizontal pixels available to this element, in panel content space. Always >= 1.

    • extraLayoutHeight

      default int extraLayoutHeight()
      Extra vertical pixels this element occupies beyond its single-line / authored baseline because it wrapped or opened. The owning Panel pushes the elements below it down by exactly this amount. Default 0.

    • fillsHeight

      default boolean fillsHeight()
      Whether this element takes its height from the panel (fillHeight(int)). Default false.

    • fillHeight

      default void fillHeight(int height)
      The height this element should occupy: the owning panel's viewport from this element's top edge down, or -1 when the panel has no viewport. Called only when fillsHeight() is true. Default: no-op.

    • isVisible

      default boolean isVisible()
      Returns whether this element is currently visible. Invisible elements are not rendered and receive no input. Default: always visible. MenuKit's elements read their builder's visibleWhen here.

    • isHovered

      default boolean isHovered(RenderContext ctx)
      Returns whether the mouse is over this element in this render pass, using the element's own bounds. false in contexts without input (HUDs).

    • tooltipSupplier

      default @Nullable Supplier<net.minecraft.network.chat.Component> tooltipSupplier()
      The element's hover-tooltip text supplier, or null if none. AbstractPanelElement returns its builder's tooltip; a direct implementor overrides this to return its own.

    • queueTooltip

      default void queueTooltip(RenderContext ctx)
      Queues this element's hover tooltip for the current frame when the cursor is over it. Routes through MKTooltip, so every element's tooltip has the library's width cap and wrap. No-op without a tooltip, without mouse input, or when not hovered.

    • render

      void render(RenderContext ctx)
      Renders this element at (ctx.originX() + getChildX(), ctx.originY() + getChildY()). When ctx.disabled() is true, an element draws its disabled look.

    • renderOverlay

      default void renderOverlay(RenderContext ctx)
      Second-pass render for transient overlays that draw outside the element's layout bounds (a Dropdown's popover). Runs after every element's render(RenderContext), so an overlay is always on top regardless of declaration order. Pairs with getActiveOverlayBounds(InputContext), the input side. Default: no-op.

    • getActiveOverlayBounds

      default int @Nullable [] getActiveOverlayBounds(InputContext in)
      The screen-space bounds [x, y, width, height] of this element's active overlay (an open popover), or null when none is open. The dispatcher gives an element whose overlay contains the event exclusive ownership of that click or scroll, before any hit test, and the claim rule treats the overlay as claimed whatever the panel's opacity.
      Parameters:
      in - the element's input context (its origin, so it can place the overlay)

    • notifyClickOutsideOverlay

      default void notifyClickOutsideOverlay(InputContext in)
      Tells an element with transient open state (a popover) that a click landed somewhere it did not claim, so it can close. The dispatchers call it on every shown element for every click, even one another element consumed; each element decides for itself whether the click was outside. Default: no-op.

    • hitTest

      default boolean hitTest(InputContext in)
      Whether this element wants the input event at the context's mouse position. Default: the element's layout bounds. Override when the interaction surface differs from the layout bounds (a container that only claims where it has children).

    • mouseClicked

      default boolean mouseClicked(InputContext in, int button)
      A mouse click on this element (the dispatcher hit-tested first). Returns true if consumed, stopping dispatch to other elements, slots and vanilla. button is GLFW's (0 left, 1 right, 2 middle). Default: false.

    • mouseScrolled

      default boolean mouseScrolled(InputContext in, double scrollX, double scrollY)
      A wheel scroll over this element (hit-tested first). Returns true if consumed. scrollY positive is up. Default: false.

    • mouseReleased

      default boolean mouseReleased(InputContext in, int button)
      A mouse release anywhere on the screen, not hit-tested, so a drag that started on the element ends wherever the cursor now is. Arrives even in a disabled context. Default: false.

    • keyPressed

      default boolean keyPressed(InputContext in, int keyCode, int scanCode, int modifiers)
      A key press, offered to every shown element of an active panel until one consumes it (keys are not pointer-localised). GLFW codes, as vanilla's GuiEventListener.keyPressed. Default: false.

    • isElementOpaque

      default boolean isElementOpaque()
      Whether this element is solid, which matters on a transparent panel: there a panel claims only its solid elements (shown, opaque and interactive). On an opaque panel the panel claims its whole rectangle (§0065). Builders set it with opaque.

    • isInteractive

      default boolean isInteractive()
      Whether this element handles pointer input, so a point on it is a solid claim on a transparent panel. Controls return true; render-only decorations keep the false default, so they never eat a click they do nothing with.

    • presentsSlotAt

      default boolean presentsSlotAt(InputContext in)
      Whether this element presents a live menu slot under the event's point. An opaque panel claims its whole rectangle; a slot the panel itself presents stays live under that claim (§0065). Default false.

    • declId

      default @Nullable String declId()
      The element's explicit, stable declaration id within its panel, or null to use its registration position in the panel's element list (the window's address for the element). Builders set it with declId.

    • onAttach

      default void onAttach(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen)
      Screen-attach lifecycle hook, called when the containing screen reaches its init(). Elements that wrap vanilla widgets register them here so vanilla's focus, keyboard and narration reach them. Default: no-op.

    • onDetach

      default void onDetach(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen)
      Screen-detach lifecycle hook, the mirror of onAttach(Screen). Default: no-op.
